ArtifactDate: 1st century BC (built under Herod the Great)
Description: The western retaining wall of the Temple Mount platform, built of massive Herodian ashlars and still standing in Jerusalem. It held up the platform on which Herod's Temple stood; it is not itself a wall of the Temple building. Excavated sections and tunnels continue to reveal its full length beneath the present city.
BiblicalSignificance: This is the closest standing stone to the Temple Jesus taught in. When the disciples marvelled at the Temple's great stones, they were looking at masonry of this scale — and when Jesus said not one stone would be left on another, the platform wall remained as a witness that the building above it was indeed thrown down.
Interpretations: Scholars agree the wall is Herod's retaining wall for the Temple platform; it is sometimes mistaken for the Temple itself, which it is not — the Temple building stood on the platform above.
